## Data S3: Supplementary File 3 ΦX174 single-amino-acid proteomic variants dataset.xlsx
```{r}

# ============================================================
# Data S3: ΦX174 single-amino-acid proteomic variants
# ============================================================

# 1. Load required packages
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)


# 2. Define supplementary data file
file_path <- paste0(
  "./codes_Github_final/Supplementary_Data/",
  "Supplementary File 3 ΦX174 single-amino-acid proteomic variants dataset.xlsx"
)

# Check file exists
stopifnot(file.exists(file_path))


# 3. Load all worksheets into a named list
sheet_names <- readxl::excel_sheets(file_path)

data_s3 <- purrr::map(
  sheet_names,
  ~ readxl::read_excel(
    file_path,
    sheet = .x,
    guess_max = 10000
  )
)

names(data_s3) <- sheet_names


# 4. Inspect loaded datasets

# Available worksheets
names(data_s3)
# [1] "WT_proteins"   "1aa_mutations" "1aa_residues" 

# Dimensions of each worksheet
purrr::map(data_s3, dim)

# Column names of each worksheet
purrr::map(data_s3, names)

# Preview first rows
purrr::map(data_s3, head)


# 5. Extract individual datasets
# Confirm exact worksheet names before running

phix_wt_proteins <- data_s3[["WT_proteins"]]

phix_1aa_mutations <- data_s3[["1aa_mutations"]]

phix_1aa_residues <- data_s3[["1aa_residues"]]


# 6. Check datasets

dplyr::glimpse(phix_wt_proteins)

dplyr::glimpse(phix_1aa_mutations)

dplyr::glimpse(phix_1aa_residues)



# ============================================================
# Fix column types in Data S3 - 1aa_mutations
# ============================================================

# Get column names from the worksheet
mutation_col_names <- names(
  readxl::read_excel(
    file_path,
    sheet = "1aa_mutations",
    n_max = 0
  )
)

# Set default column types to automatic
mutation_col_types <- rep(
  "guess",
  length(mutation_col_names)
)

# Force structural annotation columns to character
character_cols <- c(
  "monomer_structural_class_resolved",
  "monomer_structural_class_predicted",
  "residue_surface_class_resolved",
  "residue_surface_class_predicted",
  "residue_structural_group_resolved",
  "residue_structural_group_predicted",
  "residue_interaction_class",
  "binder_genes",
  "binder_classes",
  "binder_complexes"
)

mutation_col_types[
  mutation_col_names %in% character_cols
] <- "text"


# Reload the worksheet
phix_1aa_mutations <- readxl::read_excel(
  file_path,
  sheet = "1aa_mutations",
  col_types = mutation_col_types,
  guess_max = 10000
)

# Update the named list
data_s3[["1aa_mutations"]] <- phix_1aa_mutations


# Verify corrected column types
sapply(
  phix_1aa_mutations[, character_cols],
  class
)

# Check structural annotations
table(
  phix_1aa_mutations$monomer_structural_class_resolved,
  useNA = "ifany"
)
#    Core Surface    <NA> 
#    4247   17346   26543 

table(
  phix_1aa_mutations$residue_surface_class_resolved,
  useNA = "ifany"
)
#             Interface Non-interface surface                  <NA> 
#                 13407                  3939                 30790 



```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Stacked bar plot - mutation counts by structural class
# ============================================================

# Function to plot stacked bar plots by counts
bar_count_stacked_proteome <- function(
    summary_df,
    class_col = Class,
    category_col = Category,
    count_col = count,
    plot_title = "Mutation Count by Class",
    fill_legend_title = "Mutation Category",
    x_order = NULL,
    facet_col = NULL,
    stat_df = NULL,
    stat_p_col = "p_value",
    stat_format = c("p", "stars"),
    stat_position = c("subtitle", "caption", "none"),
    label_size = 3.5,
    label_color = "black",
    label_vjust = 0,
    label_offset_frac = 0.03,
    y_expand_frac = 0.15
) {
  
  stat_format   <- match.arg(stat_format)
  stat_position <- match.arg(stat_position)
  
  # ---- Symbols ----
  class_sym    <- rlang::ensym(class_col)
  category_sym <- rlang::ensym(category_col)
  count_sym    <- rlang::ensym(count_col)
  facet_sym    <- if (!is.null(facet_col)) rlang::ensym(facet_col) else NULL
  
  class_name    <- rlang::as_name(class_sym)
  category_name <- rlang::as_name(category_sym)
  count_name    <- rlang::as_name(count_sym)
  
  # ---- Grouping variables ----
  grouping_vars <- if (is.null(facet_sym)) {
    list(class_sym, category_sym)
  } else {
    list(facet_sym, class_sym, category_sym)
  }
  
  group_class_vars <- if (is.null(facet_sym)) {
    list(class_sym)
  } else {
    list(facet_sym, class_sym)
  }
  
  # ---- Clean and aggregate ----
  summary_df <- summary_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(!!class_sym),
      !is.na(!!category_sym)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(!!!grouping_vars) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      !!count_sym := sum(!!count_sym, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  # ---- Category order ----
  summary_df[[category_name]] <- factor(
    summary_df[[category_name]],
    #levels = c("Beneficial", "Neutral", "Detrimental", "Lethal"),
    levels = c(
      "Increased",
      "No effect",
      "Detrimental",
      "Strongly detrimental"
    ),
    ordered = TRUE
  )
  
  # ---- Total counts per bar ----
  totals_df <- summary_df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(!!!group_class_vars) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      total_count = sum(!!count_sym, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  # ---- X-axis ordering ----
  if (!is.null(x_order)) {
    
    summary_df <- summary_df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        !!class_sym := factor(.data[[class_name]], levels = x_order)
      )
    
    totals_df <- totals_df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        !!class_sym := factor(.data[[class_name]], levels = x_order)
      )
    
  } else if (is.null(facet_sym)) {
    
    class_order <- summary_df %>%
      dplyr::group_by(!!class_sym) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(
        order_val = sum(
          ifelse(
            .data[[category_name]] %in% c("Detrimental", "Strongly detrimental"),
            .data[[count_name]],
            0
          ),
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(order_val)) %>%
      dplyr::pull(!!class_sym)
    
    summary_df <- summary_df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        !!class_sym := factor(.data[[class_name]], levels = class_order)
      )
    
    totals_df <- totals_df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        !!class_sym := factor(.data[[class_name]], levels = class_order)
      )
  }
  
  # ---- Y-axis label position ----
  y_max <- max(totals_df$total_count, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  if (!is.finite(y_max) || y_max == 0) {
    y_max <- 1
  }
  
  totals_df <- totals_df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      label_y = total_count + label_offset_frac * y_max
    )
  
  # ---- Base plot ----
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    summary_df,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = .data[[class_name]],
      y = .data[[count_name]],
      fill = .data[[category_name]]
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_bar(
      stat = "identity",
      position = "stack",
      width = 0.9,
      color = "black"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
      data = totals_df,
      ggplot2::aes(
        x = .data[[class_name]],
        y = label_y,
        label = scales::comma(total_count)
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      size = label_size,
      color = label_color,
      vjust = label_vjust
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        #"Beneficial"  = "#A1A9D0",
        #"Neutral"     = "#D9D9D9",
        #"Detrimental" = "#F4A6A6",
        #"Lethal"      = "#F0988C"
        
        "Increased"="#A1A9D0",
        "No effect"="#D9D9D9",
        "Detrimental"="#F4A6A6",
        "Strongly detrimental"="#F0988C"
      ),
      name = fill_legend_title,
      drop = FALSE
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 5),
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
      ylim = c(0, y_max * (1 + y_expand_frac))
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = plot_title,
      x = "Class",
      y = "Mutation count"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_classic() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    )
  
  # ---- Faceting ----
  if (!is.null(facet_sym)) {
    p <- p +
      ggplot2::facet_wrap(
        vars(!!facet_sym),
        scales = "free_x"
      )
  }
  
  # ---- External statistics ----
  if (!is.null(stat_df) &&
      stat_position != "none" &&
      is.null(facet_sym)) {
    
    if (!stat_p_col %in% colnames(stat_df)) {
      stop("stat_p_col not found in stat_df.")
    }
    
    p_val <- stat_df[[stat_p_col]][1]
    
    if (stat_format == "p") {
      stat_label <- ifelse(
        p_val < 2.2e-16,
        "p < 2.2e-16",
        paste0("p = ", signif(p_val, 3))
      )
    } else {
      stat_label <- dplyr::case_when(
        p_val < 0.001 ~ "***",
        p_val < 0.01  ~ "**",
        p_val < 0.05  ~ "*",
        TRUE ~ "ns"
      )
    }
    
    if (stat_position == "subtitle") {
      p <- p +
        ggplot2::labs(
          subtitle = paste0("Chi-square test: ", stat_label)
        )
    } else if (stat_position == "caption") {
      p <- p +
        ggplot2::labs(
          caption = paste0("Chi-square test: ", stat_label)
        )
    }
  }
  
  return(p)
}
```

### 2) Ridgeline plot, mutational effect distributions (Fig. 2B)
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Function: Ridgeline distribution of replication scores
# Required packages: dplyr, ggplot2, ggridges, rlang
# ============================================================

plot_ridgeline_mut_class <- function(
    data,
    score_col = replication_score,
    class_col = aa_mut_gene,
    group_col = NULL,
    y_order = NULL,
    group_order = NULL,
    plot_title = "Ridgeline Density Plot",
    x_label = "Replication score",
    y_label = "Protein"
) {

  # ---- Capture tidy evaluation symbols ----
  score_sym <- rlang::ensym(score_col)
  class_sym <- rlang::ensym(class_col)

  group_sym <- if (!is.null(group_col)) {
    rlang::ensym(group_col)
  } else {
    NULL
  }

  class_name <- rlang::as_name(class_sym)
  group_name <- if (!is.null(group_sym)) {
    rlang::as_name(group_sym)
  } else {
    NULL
  }

  # ---- Apply manual y-axis order ----
  if (!is.null(y_order)) {

    data <- data %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        !!class_sym := factor(
          .data[[class_name]],
          levels = y_order
        )
      )
  }

  # ---- Apply manual facet order ----
  if (!is.null(group_name) && !is.null(group_order)) {

    data <- data %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        !!group_sym := factor(
          .data[[group_name]],
          levels = group_order
        )
      )
  }

  # ---- Build ridgeline plot ----
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = !!score_sym,
      y = !!class_sym
    )
  ) +
    ggridges::geom_density_ridges(
      scale = 1.2,
      fill = "grey80",
      color = "black",
      alpha = 0.8,
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::xlim(-1, 1.5) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = plot_title,
      x = x_label,
      y = y_label
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_classic() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold"
      ),
      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold"
      )
    )

  # ---- Add faceting ----
  if (!is.null(group_name)) {

    p <- p +
      ggplot2::facet_wrap(
        ggplot2::vars(!!group_sym),
        scales = "free_x",
        nrow = 1
      )
  }

  return(p)
}
```

### 3) Heatmaps, mutational effect landscapes (Fig. 2C; Fig. S2A)
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Function: Amino-acid mutational heatmap with WT markers
# Required packages: dplyr, ggplot2, scales
# ============================================================

plot_heatmap_colored_wt <- function(
    data,
    pos_col = "aa_mut_pos",
    sub_col = "aa_mut_sub",
    wt_col = "aa_mut_wt",
    value_col = "replication_score",
    wt_value = 1,
    plot_title = "",
    show_legend = FALSE,
    show_title = FALSE,
    x_tick_step = 10,
    x_text_size = 8,
    x_tick_length = 2.5,
    x_label = "Position",
    y_label = "Mutant AA"
) {

  # ---- Check required columns ----
  stopifnot(
    all(
      c(pos_col, sub_col, wt_col, value_col) %in%
        names(data)
    )
  )

  # ---- 1. Create WT rows ----
  wt_rows <- data %>%
    dplyr::distinct(
      .data[[pos_col]],
      .data[[wt_col]]
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      !!sub_col := .data[[wt_col]],
      !!value_col := wt_value
    )

  # ---- 2. Combine WT and mutant data ----
  data_plot <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    data,
    wt_rows
  )

  # ---- 3. Calculate x-axis breaks ----
  x_min <- min(data_plot[[pos_col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  x_max <- max(data_plot[[pos_col]], na.rm = TRUE)

  x_breaks <- seq(
    from = ceiling(x_min / x_tick_step) * x_tick_step,
    to = floor(x_max / x_tick_step) * x_tick_step,
    by = x_tick_step
  )

  # ---- 4. Build heatmap ----
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    data_plot,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = .data[[pos_col]],
      y = .data[[sub_col]],
      fill = .data[[value_col]]
    )
  ) +

    ggplot2::geom_tile(
      width = 1,
      height = 1,
      color = "white",
      linewidth = 0.1
    ) +

    ggplot2::coord_fixed() +

    # WT markers
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = wt_rows,
      ggplot2::aes(
        x = .data[[pos_col]],
        y = .data[[sub_col]]
      ),
      shape = 4,
      size = 0.4,
      color = "black",
      stroke = 0.4,
      inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +

    # X-axis
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
      expand = c(0, 0),
      breaks = x_breaks,
      minor_breaks = NULL,
      guide = ggplot2::guide_axis(
        check.overlap = TRUE
      )
    ) +

    # Y-axis
    ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +

    # Original replication-score color scale
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradientn(
      colors = c(
        "darkred",
        "red",
        "gray88",
        "blue"
      ),
      values = scales::rescale(
        c(-1, 0, 1, 1.5)
      ),
      limits = c(-1, 1.5),
      name = value_col,
      na.value = "white",
      guide = if (show_legend) {
        ggplot2::guide_colorbar(
          barwidth = 10,
          barheight = 1,
          direction = "horizontal",
          ticks.colour = "black",
          title.position = "top",
          title.hjust = 0.5
        )
      } else {
        "none"
      }
    ) +

    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

    ggplot2::theme(
      axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(
        size = x_text_size,
        angle = 0,
        hjust = 0.5,
        vjust = 1,
        margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 3)
      ),

      axis.ticks.x = ggplot2::element_line(
        linewidth = 0.4,
        color = "black"
      ),

      axis.ticks.length.x = grid::unit(
        x_tick_length,
        "pt"
      ),

      axis.line.x = ggplot2::element_line(
        linewidth = 0.4,
        color = "black"
      ),

      axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 12,
        margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 8)
      ),

      axis.title.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),

      panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),

      legend.position = if (show_legend) "top" else "none",

      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(
        hjust = 0.5,
        size = 14,
        face = "bold"
      ),

      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
        10, 10, 10, 10
      )
    )

  if (show_title) {
    p <- p + ggplot2::ggtitle(plot_title)
  }

  if (!is.null(x_label)) {
    p <- p + ggplot2::xlab(x_label)
  }

  if (!is.null(y_label)) {
    p <- p + ggplot2::ylab(y_label)
  }

  return(p)
}

# ============================================================
# Function: Binary structural annotation heatmap
# Required packages: dplyr, ggplot2, grid
# ============================================================

plot_heatmap_binary_class <- function(
    data,
    pos_col = "pos",
    class_col = "Class",
    value_col = "Value",
    plot_title = "",
    show_legend = FALSE,
    show_title = FALSE,
    x_tick_step = 10,
    x_label = "Position",
    y_label = "Class",
    core_color = "#a6b6c7",
    interface_color = "#aac6b0",
    absent_color = "gray95"
) {

  # ---- Check columns ----
  stopifnot(
    all(
      c(pos_col, class_col, value_col) %in%
        names(data)
    )
  )

  # ---- X-axis breaks ----
  x_breaks <- sort(unique(data[[pos_col]]))
  x_breaks <- x_breaks[
    x_breaks %% x_tick_step == 0
  ]

  # ---- Prepare fill categories ----
  plot_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      fill_class = dplyr::case_when(
        .data[[class_col]] == "Core" &
          .data[[value_col]] > 0 ~ "Core",

        .data[[class_col]] == "Interface" &
          .data[[value_col]] > 0 ~ "Interface",

        is.na(.data[[value_col]]) ~ NA_character_,

        TRUE ~ "Absent"
      ),

      fill_class = factor(
        fill_class,
        levels = c(
          "Interface",
          "Core",
          "Absent"
        )
      )
    )

  # ---- Plot ----
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    plot_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = .data[[pos_col]],
      y = .data[[class_col]],
      fill = fill_class
    )
  ) +

    ggplot2::geom_tile(
      width = 1,
      height = 1,
      color = "white"
    ) +

    ggplot2::coord_fixed() +

    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
      expand = c(0, 0),
      breaks = x_breaks
    ) +

    ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +

    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "Interface" = interface_color,
        "Core" = core_color,
        "Absent" = absent_color
      ),
      na.value = "white",
      name = "Class",
      guide = if (show_legend) {
        ggplot2::guide_legend(
          title.position = "top",
          title.hjust = 0.5
        )
      } else {
        "none"
      }
    ) +

    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

    ggplot2::theme(
      axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.title.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),

      axis.ticks.length = grid::unit(0, "pt"),

      panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),

      legend.position = if (show_legend) "top" else "none",

      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(
        hjust = 0.5,
        size = 14,
        face = "bold"
      ),

      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
        10, 10, 10, 10
      )
    )

  if (show_title) {
    p <- p + ggplot2::ggtitle(plot_title)
  }

  p <- p +
    ggplot2::xlab(x_label) +
    ggplot2::ylab(y_label)

  return(p)
}
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Stacked bar plot - structural classification by protein
# ============================================================

# Function to show mechanistic classification of detrimental mutations
bar_percent_stacked_protein_factor <- function(
  data,
  factor_col,
  count_col = count,
  palette = NULL,
  title = "Percentage within each gene",
  legend_title = "Class",
  show_legend = TRUE,
  x_order = NULL,
  order_by = "Interface"
) {

  factor_sym <- rlang::ensym(factor_col)
  count_sym  <- rlang::ensym(count_col)

  factor_name <- rlang::as_name(factor_sym)
  count_name  <- rlang::as_name(count_sym)

  # --- Step 1: Aggregate counts ---
  percent_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(!!factor_sym)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(aa_mut_gene, !!factor_sym) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      !!count_sym := sum(!!count_sym, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # --- Step 2: Ensure all x_order + factor levels exist ---
  if (!is.null(x_order)) {

    factor_levels <- if (!is.null(palette) && !is.null(names(palette))) {
      names(palette)
    } else {
      unique(percent_data[[factor_name]])
    }

    percent_data <- percent_data %>%
      tidyr::complete(
        aa_mut_gene = x_order,
        !!factor_sym := factor_levels,
        fill = setNames(list(0), count_name)
      )
  }

  # --- Step 3: Recalculate percentages ---
  percent_data <- percent_data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(aa_mut_gene) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      total = sum(.data[[count_name]], na.rm = TRUE),
      percent = dplyr::if_else(
        total > 0,
        100 * .data[[count_name]] / total,
        0
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  # --- Step 4: Total counts ---
  total_df <- percent_data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(aa_mut_gene) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      total_count = sum(.data[[count_name]], na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  if (!is.null(x_order)) {
    total_df <- tibble::tibble(aa_mut_gene = x_order) %>%
      dplyr::left_join(total_df, by = "aa_mut_gene") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(total_count = tidyr::replace_na(total_count, 0))
  }

  # --- Step 5: Factor levels ---
  if (!is.null(palette) && !is.null(names(palette))) {
    percent_data[[factor_name]] <- factor(
      percent_data[[factor_name]],
      levels = names(palette)
    )
  }

  # --- Step 6: X ordering ---
  if (!is.null(x_order)) {

    percent_data <- percent_data %>%
      dplyr::mutate(aa_mut_gene = factor(aa_mut_gene, levels = x_order))

    total_df <- total_df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(aa_mut_gene = factor(aa_mut_gene, levels = x_order))

  } else {

    order_df <- percent_data %>%
      dplyr::filter(.data[[factor_name]] == order_by) %>%
      dplyr::select(aa_mut_gene, percent)

    percent_data <- percent_data %>%
      dplyr::left_join(order_df, by = "aa_mut_gene", suffix = c("", "_order")) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(percent_order = tidyr::replace_na(percent_order, -1)) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        aa_mut_gene = forcats::fct_reorder(aa_mut_gene, percent_order, .desc = TRUE)
      )

    total_df <- total_df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        aa_mut_gene = factor(aa_mut_gene, levels = levels(percent_data$aa_mut_gene))
      )
  }

  # --- Step 7: Plot ---
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    percent_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = aa_mut_gene,
      y = percent,
      fill = .data[[factor_name]]
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_bar(
      stat = "identity",
      width = 0.9,
      color = "black"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
      data = total_df,
      ggplot2::aes(
        x = aa_mut_gene,
        y = 103,   # safe position above bars
        label = scales::comma(total_count)
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      size = 3.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 110)) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = title,
      x = "Gene",
      y = "Proportion (%)",
      fill = if (show_legend) legend_title else NULL
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_classic() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      legend.position = if (show_legend) "right" else "none",
      axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    )

  # --- Step 8: Palette ---
  if (!is.null(palette)) {
    p <- p + ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
      values = palette,
      drop = FALSE,
      na.value = "white"
    )
  }

  return(p)
}
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Data S3: Structural odds-ratio analysis
# ============================================================

# 1. Analysis datasets
phix_proteome_mut_data_advanced_list <- list(
  all = phix_1aa_mutations,

  single_orf = phix_proteome_dms_mut_missense_analysis
)

# ============================================================
# Function: Calculate Fisher's exact test odds ratio
# Corrected for character column names
# ============================================================

run_odds_ratio <- function(
    df,
    exposure_col,
    exposure_focus,
    outcome_col,
    outcome_focus,
    dataset = NA_character_,
    group = NA_character_
) {

  # Column names are supplied as strings
  exposure_name <- exposure_col
  outcome_name <- outcome_col

  # Check required columns
  stopifnot(
    exposure_name %in% names(df),
    outcome_name %in% names(df)
  )

  # Filter complete cases and define binary variables
  dat <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(.data[[exposure_name]]),
      !is.na(.data[[outcome_name]])
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      exposure = .data[[exposure_name]] == exposure_focus,
      outcome = .data[[outcome_name]] %in% outcome_focus
    )

  # Construct contingency table
  tab <- table(dat$exposure, dat$outcome)

  # Return NA if not a complete 2x2 table
  if (!identical(dim(tab), c(2L, 2L))) {

    return(
      tibble::tibble(
        test_type = "fisher_odds_ratio",
        dataset = dataset,
        group = group,
        exposure_var = exposure_name,
        outcome_var = outcome_name,
        exposure_focus = exposure_focus,
        outcome_focus = paste(outcome_focus, collapse = ","),

        n_total = nrow(dat),

        a_exposed_outcome = NA_integer_,
        b_exposed_no_outcome = NA_integer_,
        c_unexp_outcome = NA_integer_,
        d_unexp_no_outcome = NA_integer_,

        odds_ratio = NA_real_,
        conf_low = NA_real_,
        conf_high = NA_real_,

        log_or_ln = NA_real_,
        log_or_log10 = NA_real_,
        log_conf_low_ln = NA_real_,
        log_conf_high_ln = NA_real_,
        log_conf_low_log10 = NA_real_,
        log_conf_high_log10 = NA_real_,

        p_value = NA_real_,
        method = "Not 2x2 - skipped"
      )
    )
  }

  # Fisher's exact test
  ft <- stats::fisher.test(
    tab,
    alternative = "two.sided",
    conf.level = 0.95
  )

  or_val <- unname(ft$estimate)
  ci_low <- unname(ft$conf.int[1])
  ci_high <- unname(ft$conf.int[2])

  # Return results
  tibble::tibble(
    test_type = "fisher_odds_ratio",
    dataset = dataset,
    group = group,

    exposure_var = exposure_name,
    outcome_var = outcome_name,

    exposure_focus = exposure_focus,
    outcome_focus = paste(outcome_focus, collapse = ","),

    n_total = sum(tab),

    a_exposed_outcome = as.integer(tab[2, 2]),
    b_exposed_no_outcome = as.integer(tab[2, 1]),
    c_unexp_outcome = as.integer(tab[1, 2]),
    d_unexp_no_outcome = as.integer(tab[1, 1]),

    odds_ratio = or_val,
    conf_low = ci_low,
    conf_high = ci_high,

    log_or_ln = log(or_val),
    log_or_log10 = log10(or_val),

    log_conf_low_ln = log(ci_low),
    log_conf_high_ln = log(ci_high),

    log_conf_low_log10 = log10(ci_low),
    log_conf_high_log10 = log10(ci_high),

    p_value = ft$p.value,
    method = ft$method
  )
}



# ============================================================
# Function: Run odds ratios across structural classes
# ============================================================

run_odds_ratio_grid <- function(
    df,
    group_col = NULL,
    exposure_col,
    exposure_focuses,
    outcome_col,
    outcome_focus
) {

  # Proteome-wide analysis
  if (is.null(group_col)) {

    return(
      purrr::map_dfr(
        exposure_focuses,
        function(focus) {

          run_odds_ratio(
            df = df,
            exposure_col = exposure_col,
            exposure_focus = focus,
            outcome_col = outcome_col,
            outcome_focus = outcome_focus,
            group = "Proteome"
          )
        }
      )
    )
  }

  # Gene-level analysis
  gene_data <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(.data[[group_col]])
    ) %>%
    split(.[[group_col]])

  purrr::imap_dfr(
    gene_data,
    function(subdf, gene_name) {

      purrr::map_dfr(
        exposure_focuses,
        function(focus) {

          run_odds_ratio(
            df = subdf,
            exposure_col = exposure_col,
            exposure_focus = focus,
            outcome_col = outcome_col,
            outcome_focus = outcome_focus,
            group = gene_name
          )
        }
      )
    }
  )
}


# ============================================================
# Function: Run complete odds-ratio pipeline
# ============================================================

run_or_pipeline <- function(
    dataset_list,
    analysis_plan,
    exposure_focus_list,
    outcome_col,
    outcome_focus,
    group_col = NULL
) {

  purrr::pmap_dfr(
    analysis_plan,
    function(subset, exposure) {

      df_use <- dataset_list[[subset]]
      focuses <- exposure_focus_list[[exposure]]

      results <- run_odds_ratio_grid(
        df = df_use,

        group_col = group_col,

        exposure_col = exposure,

        exposure_focuses = focuses,

        outcome_col = outcome_col,

        outcome_focus = outcome_focus
      )

      results %>%
        dplyr::mutate(
          subset = subset,
          exposure_set = exposure
        )
    }
  )
}

# ============================================================
# Function: Forest plot of odds ratios
# ============================================================

plot_forest_or_raw <- function(
    data,
    label_col,
    or_col,
    low_col,
    high_col,
    p_col = NULL,
    facet_col = NULL,
    title = "Odds Ratio",
    ref_line = 1,
    or_ticks = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8),
    point_size = 2,
    ci_width = 0.6,
    star_size = 4,
    star_offset = 0.05
) {

  # ---- Build plotting dataframe ----
  df <- data.frame(
    label = as.character(data[[label_col]]),
    or = data[[or_col]],
    low = data[[low_col]],
    high = data[[high_col]]
  )

  if (!is.null(p_col) && p_col %in% names(data)) {
    df$pval <- data[[p_col]]
  }

  if (!is.null(facet_col) && facet_col %in% names(data)) {
    df$facet <- data[[facet_col]]
  }

  # ---- Keep valid log-scale values ----
  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      is.finite(or),
      is.finite(low),
      is.finite(high),
      or > 0,
      low > 0,
      high > 0
    )

  if (nrow(df) == 0) {
    stop("No valid odds ratios and confidence intervals to plot.")
  }

  # ---- Order labels ----
  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(or))

  df$label <- factor(
    df$label,
    levels = rev(unique(df$label))
  )

  # ---- Statistical significance ----
  if ("pval" %in% names(df)) {

    df$star <- dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(df$pval) ~ "",
      df$pval <= 0.001 ~ "***",
      df$pval <= 0.01 ~ "**",
      df$pval <= 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ ""
    )

  } else {
    df$star <- ""
  }

  df$star_x <- df$high * (1 + star_offset)

  # ---- Forest plot ----
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    df,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = or,
      y = label
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(
      xintercept = ref_line,
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "gray50"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_errorbar(
      ggplot2::aes(
        xmin = low,
        xmax = high
      ),
      orientation = "y",
      width = 0,
      linewidth = ci_width
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      size = point_size
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_log10(
      breaks = or_ticks,
      labels = or_ticks
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      x = "Odds ratio",
      y = NULL,
      title = title
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_classic()

  # ---- Significance stars ----
  if ("pval" %in% names(df)) {

    p <- p +
      ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(
          x = star_x,
          label = star
        ),
        hjust = 0,
        size = star_size,
        fontface = "bold"
      )
  }

  # ---- Optional faceting ----
  if ("facet" %in% names(df)) {

    p <- p +
      ggplot2::facet_wrap(
        ~ facet,
        scales = "free_y"
      )
  }

  return(p)
}
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Function: Convert class summaries into scatter plotting data
# ============================================================

prepare_scatter_from_summary <- function(
    df,
    gene_col = "aa_mut_gene",
    class_col = "residue_structural_group_predicted",
    value_col = "percent",
    classes = c(
      "Core",
      "Interface",
      "Unknown structure",
      "Non-interface surface"
    )
) {

  plot_data <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(.data[[gene_col]]),
      !is.na(.data[[class_col]]),
      .data[[class_col]] %in% classes
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(
      .data[[gene_col]],
      .data[[class_col]]
    ) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      value = sum(.data[[value_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      gene = as.character(.data[[gene_col]]),
      class = as.character(.data[[class_col]]),
      value = value
    ) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
      names_from = class,
      values_from = value
      # Missing categories remain NA
    )

  # Add completely absent class columns as NA
  for (class_name in classes) {
    if (!class_name %in% names(plot_data)) {
      plot_data[[class_name]] <- NA_real_
    }
  }

  plot_data %>%
    dplyr::select(
      gene,
      dplyr::all_of(classes)
    )
}

generate_proportion_summary <- function(
    df,

    category_col,
    positive_classes,
    output_label = "Detrimental"
) {

  stopifnot(
    all(
      c(gene_col, structure_col, category_col) %in%
        names(df)
    )
  )

  df %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(.data[[gene_col]]),
      !is.na(.data[[structure_col]]),
      !is.na(.data[[category_col]])
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      target_class = dplyr::if_else(
        .data[[category_col]] %in% positive_classes,
        output_label,
        "Other"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(
      .data[[gene_col]],
      .data[[structure_col]]
    ) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      total_n = dplyr::n(),

      positive_n = sum(
        target_class == output_label,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

      proportion = positive_n / total_n,

      percent = round(proportion * 100, 2),

      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# ============================================================

# ============================================================
# Function: Scatter plot comparing structural classes
# ============================================================

plot_core_vs_surface <- function(
    df,
    x_col,
    y_col,
    label_col = "gene",
    x_label = NULL,
    y_label = NULL,
    point_size = 1.5,
    label_vjust = -0.5
) {

  stopifnot(
    all(c(x_col, y_col, label_col) %in% names(df))
  )

  # Keep complete observations
  plot_df <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(.data[[x_col]]),
      !is.na(.data[[y_col]])
    )

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    plot_df,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = .data[[x_col]],
      y = .data[[y_col]]
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      size = point_size
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_abline(
      slope = 1,
      intercept = 0,
      linetype = "dashed"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
      ggplot2::aes(
        label = .data[[label_col]]
      ),
      vjust = label_vjust
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(0, 100),
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0, 100),
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    ggplot2::coord_fixed(
      ratio = 1
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_classic() +
    ggplot2::labs(
      x = if (is.null(x_label)) x_col else x_label,
      y = if (is.null(y_label)) y_col else y_label
    )

  return(p)
}



# ============================================================
# Generate scatter plots for both analyses
# ============================================================

# Structural class comparisons
structural_comparisons <- list(
  core_interface = c("Core", "Interface"),

  core_surface = c("Core", "Non-interface surface"),

  interface_surface = c("Interface", "Non-interface surface")
)


# Helper function to generate the three plots
generate_structural_scatter_plots <- function(
    df,
    axis_prefix = ""
) {

  lapply(
    structural_comparisons,
    function(classes) {

      plot_core_vs_surface(
        df = df,

        x_col = classes[1],
        y_col = classes[2],

        x_label = paste0(
          axis_prefix,
          classes[1],
          ")"
        ),

        y_label = paste0(
          axis_prefix,
          classes[2],
          ")"
        )
      )
    }
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Analysis 1: Distribution of detrimental mutations
# ------------------------------------------------------------

scatter_detrimental_distribution <-
  generate_structural_scatter_plots(
    df =
      summary_class_proportion_proteome_mis_mut_advanced_deleterious_plotting,

    axis_prefix = "% of detrimental mutations ("
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Analysis 2: Fraction detrimental within each class
# ------------------------------------------------------------

scatter_detrimental_fraction <-
  generate_structural_scatter_plots(
    df =
      summary_proportion_proteome_mis_mut_advanced_deleterious_plotting,

    axis_prefix = "% detrimental mutations ("
  )


# Inspect plots
print(scatter_detrimental_distribution$core_interface)
print(scatter_detrimental_distribution$core_surface)
print(scatter_detrimental_distribution$interface_surface)

print(scatter_detrimental_fraction$core_interface)
print(scatter_detrimental_fraction$core_surface)
print(scatter_detrimental_fraction$interface_surface)



# ============================================================
# Spearman correlations across structural classes
# ============================================================

calculate_structural_correlations <- function(df) {

  purrr::imap_dfr(
    structural_comparisons,
    function(classes, comparison_name) {

      x_col <- classes[1]
      y_col <- classes[2]

      # Include only proteins with both structural classes
      complete_df <- df %>%
        dplyr::filter(
          !is.na(.data[[x_col]]),
          !is.na(.data[[y_col]])
        )

      n <- nrow(complete_df)

      if (
        n < 3 ||
        dplyr::n_distinct(complete_df[[x_col]]) < 2 ||
        dplyr::n_distinct(complete_df[[y_col]]) < 2
      ) {
        return(
          tibble::tibble(
            comparison = comparison_name,
            n = n,
            rho = NA_real_,
            S = NA_real_,
            p_value = NA_real_
          )
        )
      }

      # Original R cor.test() behavior
      test <- stats::cor.test(
        complete_df[[x_col]],
        complete_df[[y_col]],
        method = "spearman"
      )

      tibble::tibble(
        comparison = comparison_name,
        n = n,
        rho = unname(test$estimate),
        S = unname(test$statistic),
        p_value = test$p.value
      )
    }
  )
}

# Analysis 1: Distribution of detrimental mutations
cor_detrimental_distribution <-
  calculate_structural_correlations(
    summary_class_proportion_proteome_mis_mut_advanced_deleterious_plotting
  )

print(cor_detrimental_distribution)
# # A tibble: 3 × 5
#   comparison            n     rho     S p_value
#   <chr>             <int>   <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>
# 1 core_interface        5 -0.3       26   0.683
# 2 core_surface          5 -0.4       28   0.517
# 3 interface_surface     8 -0.0476    88   0.935


# Analysis 2: Fraction detrimental within each class
cor_detrimental_fraction <-
  calculate_structural_correlations(
    summary_proportion_proteome_mis_mut_advanced_deleterious_plotting
  )

print(cor_detrimental_fraction)
# # A tibble: 3 × 5
#   comparison            n   rho        S p_value

# 2 core_surface          5 0.9   2.00e+ 0  0.0833
# 3 interface_surface     8 0.714 2.4 e+ 1  0.0576
```
